subject: POC trial success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@atlas-payments.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial success criteria & next steps

Thanks for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a clear plan for the POC/trial. Please confirm any changes and ownership so we can lock dates.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: Improve customer support automation for transaction disputes and reduce manual triage time.
- Volume: ~1.2M messages/month; pilot scope: 10k messages/day (~140 req/s peak).
- Sensitive data: tokens include customer PII; will run on Redwood Dedicated (VPC).

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (initial)
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 300ms per request (end-to-end).
- Throughput: sustain 500 req/s for burst windows; baseline 150 req/s steady.
- Cost: target inference cost <= $0.0005 per token (model + infra).
- Quality: intent-classification accuracy >= 92% on holdout set; entity extraction F1 >= 0.88; human QA pass-rate >= 90% for sampled responses.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and SLA for availability during pilot window.

Evaluation plan (high level)
- Redwood provides a pre-configured evaluation harness + sample harness (see attached poc-eval-plan.xlsx).
- Atlas provides representative dataset (anonymized) and owner for labeling/QA (Priya suggested).
- Metrics collection: logs + traces forwarded to your monitoring; Redwood will provide dashboards and per-route breakdowns.

Timeline / owners
- Confirm dataset & NDA: by Fri 14 Jun (Atlas, Priya owner).
- Prep & infra setup: Redwood (Marissa) — target 1 week after dataset confirmed (ready by 21 Jun).
- Trial window: 2 weeks active testing starting 24 Jun — run benchmarks and QA.
- Evaluation & decision: 1 week after trial ends.

Next steps
1) confirm dataset owner and provide anonymized sample by 14 Jun
2) review the attached poc-eval-plan.xlsx and call out any missing metrics
3) schedule a 30-min kickoff for 24 Jun to validate infra and run a smoke test

Attachments:
- poc-eval-plan.xlsx (POC evaluation checklist + KPI spreadsheet)

Thanks — happy to adjust numbers if your load/profile differs.

— Jordan

Subject: Re: POC trial success criteria & next steps

Thanks Jordan — this is a great start. A couple quick clarifications before we confirm:
1) Latency profile: the 300ms P95 — is that for cold requests or after KV/prefix caching? Our live traffic has many short context requests (avg tokens ~40).
2) Throughput: our peak windows can spike to ~600 rps for short durations (promo windows). Can Redwood handle short 5–10 minute spikes without failover?

Also Priya will be the dataset owner, and she asked if you can provide the data-anonymization checklist.

Samir
VP Product, Atlas Payments
samir.shah@atlas-payments.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@atlas-payments.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial success criteria & next steps

Great questions — answers inline below and a few clarifications to make acceptance criteria measurable:

1) Latency: the 300ms P95 target assumes warm execution with KV/prefix caching applied. For cold starts (first token where model weights may be paged in) we expect higher tail latencies; we will measure both warm P95 and cold P99 during the trial. Expected warm P95 <= 300ms, cold P99 <= 1.2s. We'll include these breakdowns in the dashboard.

2) Throughput: Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling rules. For short promo spikes up to 600 rps for 5–10 minutes we recommend enabling burst policy (we'll pre-warm capacity) — Marissa will handle the runbook. If you expect sustained peaks > 10 minutes we should provision additional reserved nodes.

Measurement & acceptance (concrete)
- Measurement window: run baseline 48-hour steady-state and one scheduled burst test during the trial.
- Quality evaluation: Atlas will label a 1k holdout set; Redwood will run blind eval and provide per-intent confusion matrices + entity-level metrics.
- Cost measurement: we will report cost/token broken down by model variant + batch profile; target is <= $0.0005/token averaged over trial (we'll capture both median and 95th percentile).

I've attached an evaluation-instructions.md that spells out dataset format and the anonymization checklist (link included). Also linking the HubSpot deal and draft evaluation doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d5e6f

If that looks good, can we confirm dataset by Fri 14 Jun and lock kickoff for Mon 24 Jun 9:00am PT?

— Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@atlas-payments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2029 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial success criteria & next steps

Technical note on benchmarking & configs (quick)
- Recommended model: opt-13b-redwood-v2 (quantized int8) for best quality/cost balance. Fallback to 6B variant for cost-constrained paths.
- Batching: use adaptive batching with max batch 64 and max latency budget 250ms to meet your P95 goals.
- KV caching: enable prefix cache for repeated sessions (we'll provide a TTL config).
- Observability: we'll push per-token latency and cost metrics to the shared dashboard. I attached benchmark-results.csv with our internal numbers on a synthetic subset — see sheet "expected_throughput".

Runbook (attached redwood-runbook.pdf) covers pre-warm steps for promo spikes and rollback procedure. Happy to run a dry-run with your infra team during the kickoff.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
